title: Batch schema sync for remote DDL in kernel bootstrap
body:
Sequential `syncSchema()` per object during bootstrap causes N×3 HTTP round-trips on remote drivers. 130 objects × 3 calls × 150ms = 58s cold start — exceeds serverless timeouts.

### Changes

- **`DriverCapabilitiesSchema` / `IDataDriver`** — New `batchSchemaSync` capability flag and optional `syncSchemasBatch(schemas)` method on the driver interface
- **`RemoteTransport.syncSchemasBatch()`** — Batches all DDL into up to 3 `client.batch()` calls (introspect tables → introspect columns → execute DDL) instead of N×3 sequential `execute()` calls. Extracted shared `buildCreateTableSQL()` helper, added `assertSafeIdentifier()` for DDL injection prevention. Does not implement internal fallback — caller handles fallback to sequential sync.
- **`TursoDriver`** — Exposes `syncSchemasBatch()` (delegates to RemoteTransport in remote mode, sequential fallback in local/replica mode), sets `batchSchemaSync: true`
- **`ObjectQLPlugin.syncRegisteredSchemas()`** — Groups objects by driver, detects `supports.batchSchemaSync`, calls `syncSchemasBatch()` when available. Falls back to sequential `syncSchema()` per object if batch is unsupported or throws at runtime

```typescript
// Before: N sequential round-trips
for (const obj of allObjects) {
  await driver.syncSchema(tableName, obj); // 2-3 HTTP calls each
}

// After: groups by driver, batched when supported
if (driver.supports?.batchSchemaSync && typeof driver.syncSchemasBatch === 'function') {
  await driver.syncSchemasBatch(batchPayload); // up to 3 batch calls total
}
```

### Backwards compatibility

- `batchSchemaSync` defaults to `false` — existing drivers unchanged
- `syncSchemasBatch()` is optional on `IDataDriver`
- SqlDriver and MemoryDriver set `batchSchemaSync: false` explicitly
- All capability test fixtures updated with the new field

> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

> <issue_title>[Performance] Batch schema sync for remote DDL in kernel bootstrap</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Problem
> 
> When running ObjectKernel bootstrap with a large number of objects (such as in world-class business suites), the schema sync (`ObjectQLPlugin.syncRegisteredSchemas`) triggers a remote DDL for each object sequentially. On remote drivers (such as Turso/libSQL in cloud mode), each table creation or alteration incurs a network round-trip per object (130+ registered objects = 260–390+ network calls).
> 
> This leads to cold start or deploy times that can exceed the default 30s-45s timeout on serverless platforms (e.g., Vercel).
> 
> ### Key evidence
> - Each object: 2–3 HTTP calls (check table, create/alter)
> - Example: 130 objects × 3 × 150ms = 58.5s on high latency
> - User-facing: Service cold boot frequently fails due to schema DDL timeouts
> 
> ## Root Cause
> The current `syncRegisteredSchemas()` loop in `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` performs a sequential await on each object's DDL. When using a remote driver (e.g. libSQL), this is highly inefficient and not tenable at cloud scale.
> 
> ## Desired Solution
> - Batch DDL: Refactor `RemoteTransport.syncSchema()` to support batching all/most DDL statements into a single `client.batch()` call if supported by the remote database.
> - Plugin architecture: Consider a `syncSchemasBatch()` API for remote/modern drivers.
> - ObjectQLPlugin: `syncRegisteredSchemas()` should detect batch support and submit all schemas in parallel or as a batch where possible.
> - Backwards compatible: Retain serial fallback for older/local/atomic drivers.
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> - Kernel cold bootstrap of 100+ objects with remote driver completes in <10s
> - No breaking change for local/dev flows
> 
> ---
> See also: [HotCRM] kernel.bootstrap timeout bug in downstream product suite.
> </issue_description>
